keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1504-1506. The Funj page: 'Founded in 1504 by the Funj people' (infobox 'Established: 1504'; Amara Dunqas reigned 1503-1533/34); Cliopatria's row begins in 1507 and the af-01-a Alodia dossier ends in 1504. The 1507 outline is carried back, less western Kordofan (442,322 km2; see the 1507 verdict); confidence 2.

Cliopatria 596,844 km2 in the gazetteer (630,271 in shapes.csv; 27.2-37.0 E, 10.9-17.95 N), corrected to 442,322 km2. Kordofan (North and South Kordufan) is not Funj land before 1755 on either page. Funj page: Kordofan 'had become a battlefield between the Funj and the Musabb'at', 'The Fur had the upper hand until 1755', when Abu Likayik 'finally managed to overrun Kordofan'. Sultanate of Darfur page: 'Over the previous centuries Kordofan had largely escaped control by any of the region's major states', 'however the Funj Sultanate centred in Sennar projected influence over eastern Kordofan via the Ghudiyat'; 'In 1734 Isawi of the Musabba'at had dislodged the Ghudiyat administration'. Cliopatria's outline holds 1,046 cells (264,533 km2) of Kordofan, 44 percent of the shape. This correction cuts Kordofan west of 30 E (about 154,500 km2) and keeps eastern Kordofan (my reading of 'eastern': 113,552 km2 east of 30 E) as influence through the Ghudiyat until the loss of 1734 (ledger), confidence 2. The Funj page gives no area. Its extent sentence ('from the Third Cataract southwards to the Ethiopian Highlands and Sobat River', 'west to Kordofan and the Nuba Mountains') is the peak (late 17th century) and fits influence in eastern Kordofan; the outline also stops at 18 N, short of the Third Cataract (the Dongola reach is added from 1523, ledger and later keyframes).

keyframe_review.note: 626,983 km2 for 1769-1819, which Cliopatria keeps whole to the end. The pages date the decline: Dongola lost to the Shaykiyya about 1782, Kordofan about 1785 (Darfur page: 'Around 1785 the Funj withdrew from Kordofan amid a civil war'), Taka after 1791, the Tigre in the later 18th century, and 'the authority of the sultanate was limited to the Gezira for good' after 1802. The keyframe states the start (with Dongola); the ledger removes the lands in turn. Kordofan is part of this shape because Abu Likayik took it in 1755; the ledger removes it in 1772, restores it in 1782 and removes it in c. 1785.

The Turco-Egyptian page: 4,000 men left Cairo in July 1820, Khartoum became the Egyptian headquarters in May 1821 and Badi VII surrendered on 14 June 1821.

ledger.note: 1504: the Funj Sultanate is founded. 'Founded in 1504 by the Funj people' with 'two accounts on the founding'; Amara Dunqas reigned 1503-1533/34. The region is Cliopatria's 1507 shape.

1504: the Funj take Alodia's remnant. Abdallah Jammah 'destroyed what was left of Alodia' and, with the Funj chief Amara Dunqas, took Soba (scholars think the Abdallabi took Soba earlier on their own); the page gives no separate year, the infobox founding is 1504.

region.text: the Nile north of the confluence of the Blue and White Niles

ledger.note: 1504: the Abdallabi become Funj vassals. Abdallab page (lead): 'they were defeated by the Funj Sultanate in 1504 and thereafter ruled over the Butana as vassals'; the Funj page has 'the Abdallabi chiefs assuming subordinate positions' at the founding. What the Funj page dates later is the grant of 'everything north of the confluence of Blue and White Nile', to be ruled 'as vassal kings of Sennar': it follows Ajib's death 'in 1611 or 1612' under Badi I, so the part north of the confluence is the 1611/12 settlement, not the 1504 one. The year is the Abdallab page's; the region (the Nile north of the confluence, with the Butana approximated by River Nile and Khartoum, as Butana is not in the gazetteer) is my reading.

region.text: the Dongola reach up to the Third Cataract

ledger.note: By 1523: the Funj hold Dongola. 'Dongola had been annexed by the recently established and Islamized Funj Sultanate with its capital Sennar by 1523' (Makuria page, which also has 'the early 16th century'). Who held the Dongola reach before is not on the page: 'It is unclear who ruled Dongola after 1366'; the Banu Kanz page says Dongola was 'captured by the tribesmen' in 1365 and does not say the Banu Kanz held it afterwards. The makuria dossier (af-01-a) names banu-kanz for its 1365 loss; this gain therefore names nobody.

region.text: the Kingdom of Fazughli, near the Ethiopian border

ledger.note: 1665: the Funj conquer Fazughli. 'In 1665 the Funj conquered the Kingdom of Fazughli.' Fazughli is placed as the Blue Nile state.

region.text: the Kingdom of Taqali in the Nuba Mountains

ledger.note: c. 1665: Taqali becomes a vassal. 'Under Badi II's rule the Funj defeated the Kingdom of Taqali to the west and made its ruler his vassal' (Funj page; Badi II reigned 1644/5-1681, so the year is a bridge). Rechecked against the Kordofan correction: Taqali lies in the Nuba Hills of South Kordufan, which the Taqali page puts 'in the Kordofan region'; it is a tributary state, not Funj rule over Kordofan (it is in the 1665 vassal tint, and the Funj lose the Ghudiyat plains in 1734). The Taqali page dates the state itself only to oral tradition (the early 16th century) or 'between 1750 and 1780', so the 1665 date rests on the Funj page alone.

region.text: eastern Kordofan (east of 30 E), where 'the Funj Sultanate centred in Sennar projected influence ... via the Ghudiyat'

ledger.note: 1734: Isawi of the Musabba'at drives out the Ghudiyat. 'In 1734 Isawi of the Musabba'at had dislodged the Ghudiyat administration and repelled subsequent Funj attempts to regain their foothold' in Kordofan (Darfur page). The Funj page has Kordofan 'a battlefield between the Funj and the Musabb'at'. The region is my reading of 'eastern Kordofan' (east of 30 E, 113,552 km2 of the Funj shape).

region.text: Kordofan, which Abu Likayik 'finally managed to overrun' and made 'his new power base'

ledger.note: 1755: Abu Likayik overruns Kordofan. 'The Fur had the upper hand until 1755, when Abu Likayik finally managed to overrun Kordofan' (Funj page); the Darfur page has 'after Isawi's death Kordofan was conquered by Abu Likaylik during his rise to power in Sennar' and gives no year. The counterpart is the Musabba'at as the Darfur page has them holding it; the Funj page names the Fur as the stronger side until then. Abu Likayik was a Funj cavalry commander (Hamaj regent from 1769), so the gain is entered for the sultanate.

1762: the Hamaj regency begins. Sennar was entered 'on 27 March 1762'; 'Badi was murdered in 1763. Thus began the Hamaj Regency' (Funj page; Hamaj page 1762-1821). The sultans remain as figureheads; the state, name and colour continue.
c. 1772: Hashim of the Musabba'at retakes Kordofan. 'Around 1772 Hashim of the Musabba'at led an insurgency which retook control of Kordofan from the aging Likaylik.'
1782: the Funj retake Kordofan. 'in 1782 the Funj (under Likaylik's son) ousted him.'
c. 1782: Dongola falls to the Shaigiya. 'Dongola finally fell to the Shaykiyya in around 1782.'

c. 1785: the Fur take Kordofan. 'Around 1785 the Funj withdrew from Kordofan amid a civil war', then 'the elderly Tayrab launched an invasion' (Darfur page, infobox 'Conquest of Kordofan: c. 1785'); the Funj page says 1785/1786 and the Hamaj page 1787.

region.text: the Tigre of what is now Eritrea

ledger.note: Second half of the 18th century: the Tigre of what is now Eritrea are lost. 'In the second half of the 18th century Sennar lost the Tigre in what is now Eritrea to the rising naib' (Funj page; the naib is of Massawa in my reading). The page gives no year (reopened for this fix); 1790 is a bridge. The page also has the Funj conquering 'north-western Eritrea' in the late 16th century; Cliopatria's outline holds only 2,529 km2 of Gash Barka, so no gain is entered.
1791: Taka makes itself independent ('after 1791 Taka around the Sudanese Mareb River made itself independent').

region.text: everything but the Gezira and Sennar

ledger.note: 1802: the Funj are confined to the Gezira. 'the authority of the sultanate was limited to the Gezira for good' after 1802. The Abdallab and Taqali pages put the tribute relations later (to 1821, see their vassal_end events), so the vassal tints run on over land the sultanate no longer rules.

region.text: the Nile north of the confluence of the Blue and White Niles

ledger.note: 1821: the Abdallabi vassalage ends with the Egyptian conquest. The Abdallab page says they ruled the Butana as vassals 'until the Egyptian conquest of 1820' and 'In 1821 Sheikh Nasir submitted to Egyptian rule without resistance'; the Funj page gives no end date but has the sultanate's authority 'limited to the Gezira for good' after 1802, so between 1802 and 1821 the vassalage is nominal.

region.text: the Kingdom of Taqali in the Nuba Mountains

ledger.note: 1821: the Taqali tribute to Sennar ends with the Egyptian invasion. Taqali page: Sennar 'was appeased by annual payments from Taqali' and 'adhered to this arrangement until the Egyptian invasion of Sennar in 1821'; the Funj page gives no end date, and has the sultanate's authority 'limited to the Gezira for good' after 1802, so the relation is nominal from then.

May 1821: the Egyptian army reaches the confluence. 'The Turks reached the Nile confluence in May 1821'; the invasion force of about 4,000 had left Cairo in July 1820 (Turco-Egyptian page) and Khartoum became its headquarters in May 1821.

14 June 1821: the last sultan surrenders. 'The last Funj sultan, Badi VII, surrendered to Ismail on 14 June' and 'the Egyptians occupied Sennar without a fight the next day' (the Hamaj page: 'Probably on 12 June').

June 1821: Egypt takes Sennar and the Gezira. 'There was no opposition from the forces of the Sultanate of Sennar, which was in a state of internal turmoil'; by early 1822 'all of riverine Sudan and Kordofan was under Egyptian control'.
14 June 1821: the Funj Sultanate ends. Infobox 'Conquered by Egypt: 14 June 1821'; annexed to Egypt Province, Ottoman Empire, 13 February 1841.

wars.name: Battle of Hannik (Funj-Ottoman frontier war)

zones.text: the Dongola reach and the Third Cataract

wars.outcome: Funj victory: the Ottomans, who had reached 'as far south as the Third Cataract', were 'crushed by the Funj at the battle of Hannik' in 1585.
wars.note: The Makuria page: the Ottomans conquered Nubia 'as far south as the 3rd cataract' in the mid-16th century.

wars.name: Funj-Ethiopian wars
wars.outcome: A full-fledged war in 1618-1619 and a Funj army of 30,000-100,000 gathered on the Dinder River in March 1744; no border change the page names.

wars.name: Shilluk raids on the Funj
wars.outcome: 'From the mid-17th century onwards the Shilluk began raiding the Funj'; no border change the page names.
wars.note: The span is the page's 'mid-17th century onwards' bridged to the late 17th century.

wars.name: Funj-Musabba'at struggle for Kordofan

zones.text: Kordofan, 'a battlefield between the Funj and the Musabb'at'

wars.outcome: The Musabba'at under Isawi dislodged the Ghudiyat administration in 1734 and 'repelled subsequent Funj attempts to regain their foothold'; Abu Likayik overran Kordofan in 1755.
wars.note: The Funj page: Kordofan 'had become a battlefield between the Funj and the Musabb'at' and 'The Fur had the upper hand until 1755'.

wars.name: Funj-Musabba'at-Fur contest for Kordofan
wars.outcome: Hashim retook Kordofan about 1772, the Funj ousted him in 1782, and about 1785 the Funj withdrew amid civil war and the Fur under Tayrab conquered it.

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: Badi VII surrendered on 14 June 1821, Kordofan fell the same year, and 'by the beginning of 1822 all of riverine Sudan and Kordofan was under Egyptian control'.
wars.note: Invasion force of about 4,000 left Cairo in July 1820; the Funj offered no opposition.

notes:
Cliopatria's single Funj row (1507..1821) is one state; start moved to 1504 (Funj page infobox and text, new keyframe) and end set to 14 June 1821 (Badi VII's surrender; annexed to Egypt 13 February 1841). The af-01-a Alodia dossier ends 1504, which this dossier follows.

Cliopatria problems: (0) KORDOFAN (fix of 2026-10-18): the outline holds Kordofan (264,533 km2, 44 percent of it) from 1507 to 1768, but the Funj and Darfur pages put Kordofan outside the sultanate until Abu Likayik overran it in 1755; the keyframes now cut Kordofan west of 30 E for 1504-1733, keep eastern Kordofan as Ghudiyat influence until Isawi's 1734 victory, have none of it for 1734-1754, and have all of it from 1755; the ledger has the 1734 loss and the 1755 gain, and the war of 1734-1755 is added. Where 'eastern' ends (30 E) is my reading; the pages name no line. (1) the shape never changes from 626-630 thousand km2 although the pages date the losses of Dongola (c. 1782), Kordofan (c. 1785), Taka (after 1791), the Tigre (later 18th century) and confinement to the Gezira (after 1802); the ledger carries them and the 1820 shape is marked adjust. (2) The northern edge (18 N) is short of the Third Cataract named as the peak limit; the Dongola reach (Funj by 1523 per the Makuria page; lost c. 1782) is added by correction in 1540-1769. (3) The Red Sea coast is not drawn: the Suakin page names no Funj rule (it dates Ozdemir Pasha's occupation to the early 1550s and the province of Habesh to 1555, the Ethiopian Empire page says 1557), so the Funj page's remark that the Ottomans occupied Sawakin 'one year later' is not placed. (4) The Makuria Kingdom row overlaps this shape 1507-1518 in Cliopatria; the makuria-kingdom dossier marks those shapes wrong.

Disagreements: Kordofan lost c. 1785 (Darfur page), 1785/1786 (Funj page), 1787 (Hamaj page); Badi VII's surrender 14 June (Funj, Turco-Egyptian) vs 'probably 12 June' (Hamaj); the Funj page's 'two accounts' of the founding; scholars think the Abdallabi took Soba before the Funj.

Confidence-1 events: Taqali (c. 1665: the Funj page gives only Badi II's reign; the Taqali page dates the state to the 18th century by some scholars) and the Tigre loss (c. 1790: the page says only 'second half of the 18th century'). The Abdallab vassalage is now 1504 to 1821 on the Abdallab page (the 1611/12 settlement north of the confluence is the Funj page's), the Taqali tribute to 1821 on the Taqali page; the Funj page's 1802 confinement to the Gezira is the end of direct rule, not of the tribute. The Dongola gain of 1523 names nobody: the Makuria page does not say who held Dongola after 1366 and the Banu Kanz page does not say the Banu Kanz did (the makuria dossier's 1365 loss to banu-kanz is therefore a reading). Region names not in the gazetteer: Butana (approximated by River Nile and Khartoum). Counterparts needing dossiers: abdallab, kingdom-of-fazughli, kingdom-of-taqali, banu-kanz, the Shaigiya, the Musabba'at (not states). No ruler list is written (the page lists nine of the reigns only). The Funj page mentions Ras al-Fil and the Benishangul-Gumuz sheikhdoms as successors; they have no Cliopatria rows.
Page budget: five pages (Funj Sultanate, Turco-Egyptian conquest, Hamaj Regency, Sultanate of Darfur, Suakin) plus Makuria (opened for makuria-kingdom).
